reviewed_by: Gemini Pro blind reviewer, batch G2-MG-Q2-Harden v2 (mat_g2_mg_q2_1), 2026-08-18

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The items successfully require students to identify and use appropriate units for both objects and distances. For example, they evaluate objects as in "Which unit would you use to measure the length of a spoon: centimeters (cm) or meters (m)?" and distances as in "The distance between the gate and the library is about 50 ___. Which unit makes the measurement reasonable: cm or m?"

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The generator successfully covers all parts of the competency: measuring "the length of an object" ("Would you measure the length of a book in centimeters (cm) or meters (m)?") and measuring "the distance between two locations" ("Which unit is best to measure the distance between the bench and the playground: centimeters (cm) or meters (m)?"). Both target units (m and cm) are well-represented as correct answers.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The vocabulary and scenarios are highly appropriate for Grade 2 students. Real-world contexts are familiar and easy to visualize, such as "length of a shoe", "pencil case", "basketball court", and the "distance between your house and the church".

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: The samples demonstrate a good variety of problem formats. Some directly ask to identify the unit for a concept ("What is the appropriate unit to measure the length of a shoe: cm or m?"), while others provide a magnitude and ask the student to infer the unit that makes sense ("A spoon has a length of about 16 ___. Which unit is correct: cm or m?").

competency_alignment.rationale: The questions strictly adhere to the competency's constraint of "(m or cm)". No out-of-scope units like millimeters or kilometers are introduced, and no numerical conversions between metric units are required. The focus remains entirely on identifying the appropriate unit as seen in "An eraser has a length of about 5 ___. Which unit is correct: cm or m?".

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The scale and numerical values used alongside the units are realistic and factually correct for the given items. For example, it correctly associates a smaller magnitude with cm for small objects ("An eraser has a length of about 5") and realistic larger magnitudes for locations measured in m ("The distance between your house and the church is about 150").
